back_blurb: Bounce, bounce, CRASH, and [Broken thing] is in three pieces. Nobody saw. [Name] could hide them under a cushion, or tell [Carer]. A warm story about a difficult little moment, finding the words to tell the truth, and what happens next.
honesty_line: Illustrated from [Name]'s photo and checked by a person before print.
cover_art: [Name] in the story's key scene from spread 1 — face large and front-on; upper third calm for the title. Hallway of a UK terrace. [Name] bounces a ball high, joyful; [Broken thing] on a shelf

title_page.spot: Small spot of the ball. No child on this page.

anchor.description: [Broken thing] on spreads 1–5, 8–10 and 12, drawn identically; the glued version with its crack from spread 8.

must_not_show: punishment, no angry face, no time-out, no lie shown working, no child touching or carrying broken pieces, no sharp or jagged edges, no glass or thin ceramic. The hiding idea appears only as a thought bubble (spread 3)

spreads.text: Bounce. Bounce. BOUNCE! [Name] is playing ball in the hall. The ball goes up to the ceiling and down to the mat. Up and down. Up and down. Higher and higher.
spreads.setting: Hallway of a UK terrace. [Name] bounces a ball high, joyful
spreads.art: Hallway of a UK terrace. [Name] bounces a ball high, joyful; [Broken thing] on a shelf
spreads.calm_zone_note: Upper left — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: Bounce… CRASH! The ball hits the shelf, and [Broken thing] wobbles, tips and falls. Crack. Now it is in three pieces on the floor.
spreads.setting: The ball has hit the shelf
spreads.art: The ball has hit the shelf; [Broken thing] in three large, clean pieces on the floor, nothing jagged; [Name] surprised, standing back
spreads.calm_zone_note: Upper — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: [Name] stands very still. The house is very quiet. A thought pops up: I could hide the pieces under a cushion. Nobody would know.
spreads.art: [Name] stands still; a thought bubble shows the pieces under a cushion
spreads.calm_zone_note: Upper right — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: Two ways, side by side. Hide the pieces. Or tell [Carer]. [Name]'s tummy feels fizzy. [Name] leaves the pieces just where they fell.
spreads.setting: [Name] stands over the pieces without touching them, hands at sides, thinking
spreads.art: [Name] stands over the pieces without touching them, hands at sides, thinking
spreads.calm_zone_note: Upper — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: [Name] walks to the kitchen, one slow step at a time. [Carer] is humming at the sink and doesn't know yet. Thump, thump goes [Name]'s heart, like a little drum.
spreads.setting: Hall to kitchen. [Name] walks slowly, empty-handed
spreads.art: Hall to kitchen. [Name] walks slowly, empty-handed; [Carer] at the sink, back half-turned, humming
spreads.anchor: [Broken thing] small in the background on the hall floor
spreads.calm_zone_note: Wall — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: "[Carer]," says [Name]. "I broke [Broken thing]. It was an accident." There. It's out.
spreads.setting: Kitchen. [Name] standing by [Carer], who has turned round
spreads.art: Kitchen. [Name] standing by [Carer], who has turned round; [Name]'s face serious
spreads.calm_zone_note: Upper — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: [Carer] kneels down, eyes soft. "[Praise words]" The fizzy feeling in [Name]'s tummy goes quiet.
spreads.setting: [Carer] kneels, soft eyes, hand on [Name]'s shoulder
spreads.art: [Carer] kneels, soft eyes, hand on [Name]'s shoulder
spreads.calm_zone_note: Upper — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: [Carer] picks up the pieces carefully. Glue on this bit. [Carer] holds it still, and [Name] counts to twenty. Some of it sticks!
spreads.setting: Kitchen table. [Carer] glues and holds the join
spreads.art: Kitchen table. [Carer] glues and holds the join; [Name] sits beside, counting on fingers, hands away from the pieces
spreads.calm_zone_note: Upper — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: One piece is too small to fix. [Name]'s face crumples. "It won't ever be the same." [Carer] nods. "No, it won't."
spreads.setting: [Carer] puts the one leftover piece into a small dish on a high shelf
spreads.art: [Carer] puts the one leftover piece into a small dish on a high shelf; [Name]'s face crumpling a little; [Carer] nodding, gentle
spreads.calm_zone_note: Upper — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: [Carer] sits down on the floor next to [Name]. "I'm sad too," says [Carer]. "And I'm glad you told me. You are much more important than [Broken thing]." [Name] leans in close.
spreads.setting: [Carer] sits on the floor beside [Name], arm round [Name]
spreads.art: [Carer] sits on the floor beside [Name], arm round [Name]; [Name] leaning in
spreads.calm_zone_note: Wall — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: At bedtime, [Carer] tucks [Name] in. "You can always come and tell me when something goes wrong," says [Carer]. [Name] smiles all the way under the duvet.
spreads.art: Bedtime. [Carer] tucks [Name] in; [Name] smiling under the duvet
spreads.anchor: [Broken thing] not shown; face check against spread 10
spreads.calm_zone_note: Wall — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: Next morning, [Broken thing] is back on the shelf, with a thin crack all the way round. [Name] looks at the crack for a long time. It is part of the story now.
spreads.setting: Morning light. [Broken thing] back on the shelf, a thin glued crack and one small missing piece visible
spreads.art: Morning light. [Broken thing] back on the shelf, a thin glued crack and one small missing piece visible; [Name] looking up at it, calm
spreads.calm_zone_note: Upper — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: At [School], [Name] knocks over the paint water. Splosh! "I did that," says [Name]. "Thank you for telling me," says the teacher. They mop it up together.
spreads.art: Nursery or school art table; tipped paint-water pot; [Name] and the teacher mop up together
spreads.calm_zone_note: Upper — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

spreads.text: Walking home, [Name] stands up very straight, as tall as a lamp post. "Telling the truth," thinks [Name], "makes me feel tall."
spreads.setting: Pavement home. [Name] stands very straight beside a lamp post
spreads.art: Pavement home. [Name] stands very straight beside a lamp post; [Carer] beside, smiling
spreads.calm_zone_note: Sky — keep low-detail; story text sits there.

parent_spread.you_could_say: "Thank you for telling me. That was brave." Thank the telling first, then sort it out together.
parent_spread.try_together: "How did [Name]'s tummy feel before telling, and after?"
parent_spread.in_real_life: Next time something breaks, say thank you for the telling before anything else. Grown-ups pick up anything sharp.
parent_spread.read_it_again: Read it a few nights in a row, and again whenever [Name] asks.
